additional_info.subject: Log Analysis Request – SID Y2/R4: 31298223001 and SID Y2/R5: 313048135001
additional_info.body:
Hello,
We are currently facing a charging issue with one of our NEOTRUCKS vehicles, which is equipped with ferrite filters and a compliant charger.
•     This vehicle had been charging successfully with the Siemens supercharger since week 34.
•     Since today, neither of the two charging stations is able to charge the vehicle.
Details of the tests carried out:
•     First attempt: Today ; around 12:00 → NOK
•     Further attempts after 15:00 (Today) :
•     1st attempt → NOK
•     2nd attempt → OK
•     3rd attempt → OK
Charging stations concerned:
•     Y2/R4: 31298223001
•     Y2/R5: 313048135001
It is important to note that this site has received very specific attention from your R&D teams (Fosco and Catalina), and several updates as well as additional filters were implemented under the supervision of your European teams.
The objective of this request is to understand why the charging did not start and to determine whether the issue originates from the truck itself or from our charging stations.
We kindly request you to analyze the logs in order to identify the root cause and advise on corrective actions.
Best regards,

additional_info.subject: ID0447722-DC/Si-D/FR-[Y2 / R4 312982230001] Log Analysis Request CRM:02699000230
additional_info.body:
Dear Malek,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0447722.
The ticket has been opened for a log analysis request on the chargers at Autorecharge/Procter&Gamble, which are charging with NEOTRUCKS EVs.
Apologies for the late answer. I checked the two chargers and the logs of the session reported on 03.09.2025, and these are my findings:
I aligned with Mora Catlina, who follows in copy, and understood that on 03.09.2025, the chargers were equipped with ferrites, and the NEOTRUCKS already performed those internal changes, that resulted beneficial in order to charge with Sicharge Ds.
On 03.09.3035, the sessions you reported were all performed on charger
Y2 / R5 313048135001.
I could not see any session performed on charger
Y2 / R4 312982230001.
For future reference, I kindly ask you to please always specify on which charger is performed each test session.
First session:
DC2 is connected at 2025-09-03T09:17:59. Session ends at 2025-09-03T09:18:52, and I cannot see any communication started between charger and vehicle, as if the vehicle is not reacting to the plug. The vehicle did not communicate even the EVMAC.
Second session:
DC2 is connected at 2025-09-03T11:16:20. Also in this case, I see no reaction from the plug-in to the vehicle. EVMAC is not communicated and session fails.
Third session:
DC2 is connected at 2025-09-03T13:31:33. Again, I see no reaction from the plug-in to the vehicle. EVMAC is not communicated and session fails.
Fourth session:
DC2 is connected at 2025-09-03T13:33:26.
Authentication Phase finally starts:
2025-09-03T13:33:37.312970+00:00 [FW080005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [DCC]  DC2: Charging Phase "P00_UNKNOWN" --> "P01_AUTHENTICATION"
EVMAC :"00.14.2d.f1.be.3f" is communicated
Session fails unexpectedly at 2025-09-03T13:33:40, with the following error "peer closed connection in SSL handshake (104: Connection reset by peer) while SSL handshaking to upstream"
Fifth session:
DC2 connected at 2025-09-03T13:33:52.
Authentication phase starts:
2025-09-03T13:34:02.809598+00:00 [FW080005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [DCC]  DC2: Charging Phase "P00_UNKNOWN" --> "P01_AUTHENTICATION"
No unexpected error by closing connection. This session finally is successful.
Sixt session:
Previous session is stopped, and DC2 is connected again at 2025-09-03T13:37:17.
Charging session goes smoothly.
In conclusion:
It seems that sometimes this EV goes into a sleeping mode, and the first time the Charger is plugged in there is no reaction from the EV. Unfortunately, EcoG logs are not available to confirm this theory.
For the first two attempts, it would have been required to plug in a second time, to verify the above theory.
I ask my colleagues Catalina and Francisco to confirm if such behavior with NEOTRUCKS was observed before.
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei
Siemens AG

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0447722-DC/Si-D/FR-[Y2 / R4 312982230001] Log Analysis Request CRM:02699000230
additional_info.body:
Hi Fosco!
“I ask my colleagues Catalina and Francisco to confirm if such behavior with NEOTRUCKS was observed before”
I can confirm your last sentence based on the first investigation which me and Sebastien Collet did some months ago, which I shared the document, that I send in attachment.
As you can see, there has been literally thousands of sessions where we see that the EVMAC is not even shared.
According to the latest investigation done by Catalina, our understanding is that the changes only improved the charging interruptions due to the TCP connection being closed. Regarding the SLAC communication failures (no EVMAC), as far as we know, there was no improvement.
I hope this helps.
With best regards,
